name: Finnu Designs
old_description: We have been adding value and style to homes, offices, restaurants, and more since 2014. We would love to work on your next project for you!
about:
Finnu Designs, based in West Fargo, North Dakota, was founded in 2014 by Josh Humble. The company began as a woodworking venture and expanded into a multidisciplinary design studio working with wood, metal, and stone.

The shop produces custom built-in cabinetry, one-of-a-kind furniture, and home goods, guiding clients through a six-step process that covers concept, creative design, planning, building, delivery, and a 30-day follow-up inspection. The team handles woodworking, metal fabrication, and stone fabrication in-house, and manages installation on site.

Finnu serves both residential and commercial customers, including homeowners, office developers, and restaurant operators. Past projects include a barn door for a private residence, a dining table for a homeowner, and collaborative work with Mosaic Design & Build on commercial interiors.

The company emphasizes a “Quality Craftsmanship Guarantee” and a culture summed up as “Once a Finnu’er, always a Finnu’er.” Every build ships with a care package, and the crew pledges to leave each job site in the same or better condition than they found it.

name: First Electronics Inc
old_description: FEI specializes in the assembly of printed circuit boards, cable and wire harnesses, and electromechanical box builds, including testing and engineering support.
about:
First Electronics Inc. operates from Chandler, Arizona, where it provides contract electronics manufacturing services. The company focuses on printed circuit board assembly, cable and wire harness fabrication, and electromechanical box builds, supported by testing and engineering expertise.

Its capabilities span surface-mount and through-hole PCB assembly, conformal coating, X-ray inspection, and pre- and post-reflow inspection. The shop handles harness assembly, electro-mechanical assembly, and piggyback component placement, accepting jobs from engineering prototypes to large-volume production runs.

The company serves customers in wind energy technology, healthcare and medical devices, and telecommunications. These sectors rely on FEI for assembled boards, cable assemblies, and complete box builds that meet industry-specific quality requirements.

FEI emphasizes that quality begins at the quoting stage and that customer satisfaction is its primary goal. It also highlights the use of advanced, customized test equipment as a differentiator for delivering reliable assemblies.

name: First Medical
old_description: You must have JavaScript enabled in your browser to utilize the functionality of this website.
about:
First Medical was founded in 1985 by Ed Gogerty and Jim in Urbandale, Iowa. The privately held company began as a supplier of urological products and expanded over the decades to serve a broader healthcare market.

Today the company operates as a distributor of medical and surgical supplies, pharmaceuticals, and equipment. It offers a range of supply-chain services including no-minimum-order purchasing, less-than-case quantities, a private-label program (Quality Choice Physician Network), no-cost initial inventory, par-level ordering, alternative product sourcing during backorders, same-day delivery, 24-hour emergency service, and custom stocking of practice-specific items. A pharmacist is on staff and phones are answered 24/7, even on holidays.

First Medical serves thousands of medical offices, physician practices, retail pharmacies, and home-healthcare providers needing oxygen and enteral products. The company is a member of Independent Medical Co-op Inc., which extends its purchasing reach.

The firm emphasizes competitive pricing and personalized service, highlighting the economical benefits of buying from a Midwestern company. Its founding goal was to provide outstanding service with competitive pricing, a promise it backs with same-day delivery and round-the-clock support.

name: First Solar Louisiana
old_description: First Solar’s roots run deep in American soil. Born in the Midwest, headquartered in the Southwest, and shipped worldwide, First Solar is an American success story. Driven by a passion for innovation and powered by American ingenuity, First Solar has consistently invested in American manufacturing and American jobs. Today, it is the only US-headquartered company among the world’s largest module producers.
about:
First Solar operates a manufacturing facility in New Iberia, Louisiana, part of a company born in the Midwest and now headquartered in the Southwest. The facility produces photovoltaic modules using the company's proprietary cadmium telluride (CdTe) thin-film technology.

The plant manufactures Series 6 and Series 7 solar modules, along with mounting components, wiring harnesses, and preformed line products. Its differentiated semiconductor process yields modules with a warranted annual degradation rate of 0.3 percent and what the company calls the industry's only cell-cracking warranty. The SpeedSlot mounting feature is designed to reduce installation time and hardware costs. Recycling solutions and post-sales support round out the offering.

The modules serve utility-scale, commercial, and residential solar projects worldwide. First Solar positions itself as the only U.S.-headquartered company among the world's largest module producers, shipping to the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, India, and Asia-Pacific.

The company emphasizes its "Responsible Solar" framework, citing the lowest carbon footprint, water footprint, and energy payback time in the industry. Its thin-film technology was developed through decades of research and capital investment, aiming to deliver more lifetime energy per nameplate watt than conventional crystalline-silicon panels.

name: First State Fabrication
old_description: Custom Fabrications — Platforms, mezzanines, supports, and custom components built to specification.
about:
First State Fabrication has operated from Seaford, Delaware since its founding in 1926. The company remains privately held, though ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication, producing stairs, railings, canopies, and custom components such as platforms, mezzanines, and supports. Processes include CNC plasma cutting, press braking, shearing, pipe and tube bending, rolling, sawing, certified welding, and in-house detailing with BIM. Equipment includes a 250-ton Accurpress press brake, Ercolina angle rolls and benders, Ellis and Marvel band saws, a Bend Tech Dragon CNC pipe and tube cutter, a 10-foot Betenbender shear, a Messer MetalMaster 5-by-10-foot CNC plasma table, and two Spydercranes (URW295 and URW547) for erection in confined spaces.

The company serves contractors, builders, and design teams across commercial construction, architectural metalwork, and industrial facilities such as wastewater treatment plants and chemical plants. Its ADA-compliant hand and guardrail systems meet IBC/ADA requirements, and its architectural steel assemblies are engineered for both decorative and functional performance.

First State Fabrication emphasizes shop-to-field accuracy, code-ready fabrication, and partnership through coordination, inspection, and on-schedule delivery. The firm also highlights its community roots in the Seaford area, supporting local organizations and events.

name: Fisher Auto Parts
old_description: In 1929, when our country was entering the great depression, Blair Coiner founded his company with high hopes, perseverance and determination.
about:
Fisher Auto Parts traces its roots to 1929 in Weston, West Virginia, when Blair Coiner founded Coiner Parts during the Great Depression. Coiner began by supplying auto parts to car dealers, service stations, and independent garages, emphasizing high-character dealer service.

The company rebranded as Fisher Auto Parts in 1983 after expanding to 60 locations and 300 employees. Today, the headquarters in Weston operates with a staff of 18, overseeing a network of retail stores and Federated Car Care Centers. Fisher distributes quality name-brand parts from major manufacturers, offering an online catalog (Federated Link Catalog), safety data sheets, technical training, and maintenance resources such as tech tips and the "Two Guys Garage Tech Talk" series.

Fisher serves the automotive aftermarket, including car dealerships, service stations, repair garages, professional technicians, and retail customers. Its store locator and car care repair center locator connect drivers and shops with local inventory and service.

Founded on perseverance and a commitment to exceeding expectations in value, quality, and service, Fisher differentiates itself through fast, dependable delivery and a focus on pleasing each customer with the service they deserve.

name: Flair USA
old_description: Vertically integrated for full product development & customer-focused innovation
about:
Flair Flexible Packaging, operating as Flair USA, is headquartered in Appleton, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1992 and remains privately held and family-owned. It began as a flexible packaging manufacturer and has grown into a vertically integrated operation with facilities across North America and Asia.

The company produces flexible packaging films, pouches, and bags through extrusion, converting, flexographic printing (up to 10 colors), solventless lamination, and rotogravure printing. Its Appleton site houses an extrusion facility, a converting facility, an analytical lab, and an application lab. The firm offers both custom-engineered structures — including coextruded and laminated films for hot-fill, high-pressure processing, and retort applications — and a stock program of unprinted rollstock, lidding, and vacuum pouches.

Flair serves food and non-food markets such as meat and poultry, seafood, cheese and dairy, prepared foods, snacks and sweets, baby food, grains and spices, fruits and vegetables, coffee and tea, liquids and spreads, pet care, and foodservice. Customers range from national brands to regional processors seeking tailored barrier performance, shelf-life extension, and sustainable formats.

The company emphasizes vertical integration as a differentiator, controlling quality from resin extrusion through final conversion. It highlights its FSSC 22000-certified food safety system, FDA/USDA/CFIA compliance, and collaborative development model that includes factory acceptance testing, shelf-life validation, and on-site engineering support.

name: Flat-To-Form Metal Specialties, Inc.
old_description: We serve many different manufacturers in Michigan and Beyond. Read what some of our clients have to say about our custom fabrication services.
about:
Flat-To-Form Metal Specialties, Inc. was founded in 1995 in Fremont, Michigan, where it operates a sheet metal fabrication shop serving manufacturers across the region and beyond. The company is privately held; no specific ownership designation such as veteran- or woman-owned is publicly stated.

The shop provides a full range of custom fabrication services, including turret punching (24 gauge to 7 gauge), shearing, forming, MIG/TIG/spot/stud welding, laser cutting, plasma cutting, tapping, press‑in fastener installation, assembly of hinges, gaskets and hardware, and custom prototyping. Materials processed include stainless steel, aluminum, cold‑rolled steel, galvanized, galvannealed, hot‑rolled pickled & oiled, and fish paper. The company handles orders from single prototypes to runs of thousands of assembled pieces, though no fixed facility size or headcount is disclosed.

Customers span general manufacturing, lubrication‑system builders (Mighty Lube Systematic Lubrication in Fremont and OPCO Lubrication Systems in West Michigan), office‑furniture makers, and gas‑pump manufacturers. The firm emphasizes delivery flexibility, offering local pickup, UPS, FedEx, and freight trucking from its Fremont location.

Flat‑To‑Form highlights its ISO 9001:2015‑certified quality system, backed by internal audits, management reviews, and annual surveillance audits, as a core differentiator. It also promotes a one‑stop‑shop model that combines punching, forming, welding, laser, plasma, assembly and finishing under one roof, plus rapid prototyping for design validation.
